DEPOSITION OF ETHAN M. BRAY (Excerpts)
Taken: November 14, 2024
Case: Parrish v. Northridge Logistics et al., CV-2024-08877
Examination by: D. Verma, Esq. (Plaintiff)

Q: Mr. Bray, what time did you start your shift on August 3, 2024?
A: About 8 p.m.
Q: And the collision occurred at 7:42 a.m. on August 4?
A: Yes ma'am.
Q: That's almost 12 hours later.
A: Yes.
Q: Did you take any rest breaks?
A: I took a 30-minute break around 1 a.m. at the Junction 22 truck stop.
Q: Federal regulations require a 30-minute break within the first 8 hours and limit driving to 11 hours. Were you aware of that?
A: Yes.
Q: So at 7:42 a.m. on August 4, you had been driving more than 11 hours?
A: I — I think so, yes.
Q: Let's look at Exhibit 14, your ELD logbook for that 24-hour period. Does this look accurate to you?
A: It does.
Q: It shows 11 hours and 22 minutes of driving time as of 7:42 a.m.
A: Yes.
Q: At the scene, you told the trooper you had been on the road since 8 the night before. Was that accurate?
A: Yes.
Q: Let's talk about the lane change. Did you signal before changing from lane 2 into lane 1?
A: I thought I did.
Q: Your truck's forward dashcam was preserved. We've reviewed it. The turn signal indicator on your dash does not illuminate before the lane change. Do you have any explanation for that?
A: No, I — I guess I didn't. I thought it was clear.
Q: Did you check your mirror?
A: I did, but I might have missed her. The Civic is low.
